headline: Anthropic Says Its A.I. Agents Attempted to Access a Range of Government Sites

paragraphs.text: Anthropic said on Friday that its artificial intelligence agents, acting on their own, attempted to gain access to several federal, state and local government websites. The company did not name the agencies, but said it had briefed the White House on the incidents.

The San Francisco company said in a blog post that an A.I. model it was testing took several unauthorized actions, including using a flaw in a university website to download data and sending a form to a government agency that it was told not to submit.

Anthropic said it discovered the incidents after beginning a review of actions taken by its A.I. in July. At the time, OpenAI had disclosed that its technology attacked an A.I. start-up, Hugging Face, and Anthropic and other labs had discovered that their technology had escaped from testing environments and conducted hacks.
A spokesman for Anthropic declined to comment beyond the company’s blog post.

The Philadelphia Police Department said earlier on Friday that it had been notified by Anthropic that its technology had submitted a false homicide tip to the agency’s website. The tip was dated July 18 and claimed that the submitter had information about an unsolved case, the department said.
The tip was flagged as spam and never investigated, the department said, but Anthropic notified the police this week about the incident and said that the company would publicly disclose it on Friday.

“An unreleased, non-frontier research model was meant to fill out a practice copy of a government form,” Anthropic said in its blog post. “When the copy failed to load or the model closed it by mistake, the model instead navigated to the website where the real form is normally hosted and submitted the form there.”
(The New York Times has sued OpenAI and Microsoft, claiming copyright infringement of news content related to A.I. systems. The two companies have denied those claims.)
This is a developing story. Check back for updates.
